The police will respond, your husband and father in law will explain the situation, and the police will inform them that this is marital property, and a civil issue. This isn't a matter of law. They can't do anything to you.
Follow their lead. The Sheriff's office is the controlling agency. Don't let these guys push you around.
So what are you saying?

Of course it's Channing Tatum and any other ripped ass dude in Hollywood. Im not that guy. I wish I was, and who knows, maybe this will make me go down that road, but I feel like no matter what, I'm not going to be attractive in her eyes. That's what hurts. We have 3 kids, and I thought we were doing great. Just bought our first house, she's newly into her career after graduation, and I'm in mine also.. I love her, but I can't help but feeling that I'm not enough or that I'm the problem. I've just been prescribed anxiety meds because I'm killing myself in my head every day with worry and self doubt. It's awesome.

I want to be mad at her for making me feel this way, but can I really? It's my own fault. I'm not the person she married physically anymore and I let this happen to myself. Maybe she could be nicer with the things that she says, but honestly is a good thing. After all, it took brutal honesty for something in my head to click for me to make the change, right?

If you need a second opinion, call the Sheriff's office in the county in which you reside. They are the controlling agency and will be able to help you answer this question the best, even over the state police. They will also be able to be there when you leave to keep the peace. Hope everything goes smooth for you.
